text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostToIga(x) ::: x lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022.
Female(x) ::: x is a female tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
Male(x) ::: x is a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
LostToRafael(x) ::: x lost to Rafael Nadal at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros(x) ::: x is at Roland Garros 2022.
Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are one of the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostToIga(x) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
∀x (Female(x) → LostToIga(x)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolandGarros(x) → (Female(x) ∨ Male(x))) ::: All tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (Male(x) → LostToRafael(x)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros in 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
(RankedHighly(coco) ∨ LostToRafael(coco)) → ¬Male(coco) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros(coco) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.
Conclusion:
¬(LostToIga(coco) ∧ ActivePlayer(coco)) ::: Coco Gauff is not both a player who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 and one of the most active players in major tennis.
